wave: cellwork member adoption + unfence lever — CodeRabbit round-1 reconciliation

findings.claim: an adoption that cannot be persisted still lets the verb call plane.handoff, so the TEAM row can reach mode=checkpoint with no cell row
findings.how: AdoptionFailure {kind:read|write, detail} surfaces through CallerContext.adoptionFailure; cellwork_handoff refuses before plane.handoff and says the TEAM checkpoint was NOT recorded
findings.pin: test/member-adoption.test.ts — an adoption the record cannot persist refuses BEFORE the team plane is touched (plane.handoffs length 0, no row persisted)

findings.claim: a fence that exists only on the TEAM record answered not-fenced and was never cleared
findings.how: decision table: CELL fenced:true = the give-up (clear the CELL row and reopen the TEAM seat through the seam); TEAM-only fenced:true = clear the plane, CELL untouched; bare TEAM mode=checkpoint = checkpoint-pending, nothing written; neither = not-fenced
findings.pin: test/dispatch-unfence.test.ts — TEAM-only explicit fence; checkpoint-pending; production-shape full recovery; no-seam honesty

findings.claim: the unfence write was built from a pre-await snapshot, so a concurrent write (e.g. a fresh adoption) could be reverted
findings.how: the record is re-read after the awaited plane calls and only the cleared rows are merged into the fresh record; the snapshot is used only when the read fails
findings.pin: test/dispatch-unfence.test.ts — a row written while the plane call is awaited survives the unfence write

findings.claim: the ASCII-only nameKey collapses non-ASCII names, so unfence could clear a different member (工程师乙 -> 工程师甲)
findings.how: one resolver: exact key, then exact display name, then the normalized key ONLY when non-empty AND unique; otherwise unknown/ambiguous and the whole call is refused. Used by unfence, cellwork_send's recipient lookup and its self guard
findings.pin: test/dispatch-unfence.test.ts + test/member-resolution.test.ts — exact CJK names, ambiguous and absent names refuse with no side effects

findings.where: docs/cellwork.md + docs/cellwork.zh-CN.md (+ the cellwork README pair)
findings.claim: the fenced-owner skip reason was documented as naming unfence, while the producer names reassign
findings.how: both languages now state that the skip reason is the TEAM PLANE's own sentence naming reassign, and never unfence
findings.pin: bun run verify:docs (parity) + the corrected paragraphs

repairRounds: r2: the unfence gate must not clear a pending checkpoint (a display predicate was authorising a destructive write)
r3: the give-up fence lives on the CELL row, not the TEAM row — the r2 gate made the lever a no-op against the production shape, and every clear-path test had manufactured a team flag
r4: supervise reported the derived barrier sentence for a production give-up and hid the recorded fencedReason; duplicate unfence names journaled twice
verification: verifier 1: FAIL on six findings (missing handoff description; adoption inside the guard predicate; the adopted marker dropped by memberAfterBarrier; supervise advising reassign; two description/doc claims)
verifier 2: PASS after the r1 repair
verifier 3: FAIL (the r2 gate disabled the lever for the production give-up; CJK send still mis-routes through seatKey — recorded as a separate defect)
verifier 4: PASS after the r3 repair (production give-up recovered on both records, probe-proven), with one Medium (supervise reason) and one Nit (duplicate names)
verifier 5: PASS after the r4 repair, three nits (one test gap, one stale wording, this evidence file)
final nits landed: a shipped arm for the TEAM-only supervise reason, and the two 'per name' sentences corrected to 'per distinct member'
bounds: All proof is offline (tool harness + the shared team-plane double); no live dsh boot, no real compaction or reseed.
The adoption recovery only covers a session the live TEAM record already knows.
The unfence lever reopens the TEAM seat only through the mpdTeamActions.unfence seam; without it the plane half is reported absent and the seat stays closed.
The adoption re-read narrows, but does not eliminate, a cross-process lost-update window before the atomic rename.

KNOWN SEPARATE DEFECT, not fixed here: the mailbox identity (seatKey) still derives from the ASCII-only nameKey, so two CJK seat names can share one mailbox address — a message addressed to one may land in the other's inbox. Pre-existing, out of this wave's scope, recorded as its own follow-up.
